title: Hosting model and deployment topology
status_rationale: Requirements fix the architecture shape (component monolith on managed PostgreSQL) but not the hosting provider, regions or compute model; the persistence design states the database engine is not yet selected.
target_answer: Unbound is hosted on a major public cloud provider selected through a documented decision (open), using managed platform services rather than self-operated servers wherever available: a managed container or application platform for the single F# deployable (REQ-X-020) and managed PostgreSQL for the authoritative store (CNV-ARC-001, CNV-ARC-004). Each sponsor is placed in a deployment cell according to its isolation profile (UNB-TEN-002). Echelon operates no data centers or physical servers. The topology, providers and regions are published in the system description and subservice organization list.
current_practice: Not established. No production hosting exists. Hosting provider, regions and managed services for Unbound are not selected (no verified production infrastructure exists as of 2026-11-25).
intended_practice: Record a hosting ADR covering provider, compute model, managed PostgreSQL service and regions, satisfying ADR-001 and ADR-008 in the persistence design.
customer_statement: Unbound has not yet been deployed. The planned design is a single application deployed on managed cloud services with managed PostgreSQL; the hosting provider has not been selected.
residual_risks: Managed services shift operational risk to providers whose controls Echelon can only assess through their reports.
open_questions: Which cloud provider, compute service and managed PostgreSQL offering will be used?
Contradiction: CNV-ARC-001 and CNV-ARC-004 assume managed PostgreSQL while TENANT-AWARE-PERSISTENCE-DESIGN.md states the database engine is not yet selected (ADR-001).
Strata supports PostgreSQL 16 only (current-state brief); does the chosen managed service offer PG16 for the support horizon Unbound needs?

title: Hardening baselines for hosts, images and managed services
status_rationale: No images, hosts or baselines exist.
target_answer: Unbound runs on minimal container images built from an approved base (distroless or minimal OS with only the .NET runtime and required native libraries), rebuilt in the pipeline on every release and at least weekly. Images run as non-root with no shell or package manager. Where hosts are visible to Echelon, they follow CIS Benchmark-aligned settings applied by the platform; for managed services, Echelon applies the provider's security configuration baseline and records deviations. Hardening settings are expressed as policy-as-code and verified at build and at admission, not by periodic manual review.
intended_practice: Define base image and managed-service baselines once the provider is chosen; add image policy checks to the release gate.
provable: Nothing. No production environment, configuration or operating evidence exists.
customer_statement: Planned: minimal, non-root container images built from an approved base and checked against hardening policy at build and deployment. Not yet implemented.
residual_risks: Minimal images reduce but do not remove native library exposure; .NET on Linux depends on OpenSSL and ICU from the base image.

title: Infrastructure patching and vulnerability remediation
status_rationale: SOC2-016 requires a vulnerability program with findings and retest evidence; nothing is operating.
target_answer: Infrastructure is patched by rebuilding, not by patching in place. Every release rebuilds images from current base images and dependencies; an automated weekly rebuild runs even without code changes. Vulnerabilities in images, the .NET runtime, NuGet packages and managed service versions are scanned on each build and daily against the deployed inventory. Remediation targets are tied to exploitability: actively exploited (CISA KEV listed) issues reachable in Unbound within days, other critical issues within 14 days, high within 30 days, with exceptions time-limited and approved (SOC2-033). Managed PostgreSQL minor versions follow the provider's maintenance window; major upgrades are gated by Strata compatibility (CNV-ARC-004).
intended_practice: Adopt scanning with the release pipeline; define SLA with exploitability weighting; record exceptions as data.
provable: Nothing. No production environment, configuration or operating evidence exists.
customer_statement: Planned: patching by automated rebuild and redeploy at least weekly, with exploitability-based remediation targets. Not yet operating.
residual_risks: Provider-managed components are patched on the provider's schedule; Echelon can only monitor, not accelerate, those patches.
open_questions: What remediation SLA will be committed contractually, and will customers accept exploitability-based rather than CVSS-only targets?

challenge.customer_intent: Customers want known vulnerabilities fixed before attackers exploit them.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Breach through an unpatched, publicly known vulnerability.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Fixed CVSS-based SLAs (for example critical in 30 days) are easy to audit but treat unreachable and reachable flaws alike, and in-place patching leaves drifted, inconsistent servers.
challenge.legally_required: Not generally. Federal civilian agencies are bound by BOD 26-04 (which replaced BOD 22-01 on 2026-06-10) for KEV entries, which does not bind Echelon. PCI DSS Req 6.3.3 sets a one-month target for critical patches where card data is in scope.
challenge.contractually_required: Bank and insurer contracts often specify CVSS-based remediation windows.
challenge.historical_convention: Monthly patch cycles date from on-premises server management.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Immutable rebuild-and-redeploy removes long-lived servers that accumulate missing patches.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Weekly automated rebuild means the default state is current, with no human step to forget.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Image digests and SBOMs per deployment show exactly what was running at any time.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Exploitability-weighted SLAs (KEV and reachability) combined with weekly rebuild.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, if the scanner, SBOM and deployment records are retained per release.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If any long-lived host or manually patched component exists, or if rebuilds fail silently.
challenge.conventional_cost: Patch management tooling and staff time for in-place patching.
challenge.alternative_cost: Pipeline compute and scanner tooling, mostly open source (for example Trivy, OSV).
challenge.alternative_risks: Reachability analysis can be wrong; a false 'unreachable' delays a needed fix.
supporting_arguments: Rebuild cadence gives a uniform, provable state.
Prioritizing exploited vulnerabilities matches how breaches occur.

agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely if the committed windows are no longer than customers' CVSS-based windows; uncertain if Echelon proposes longer windows for unreachable findings.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Auditors may still sample CVSS SLA adherence and treat reachability exceptions as deviations.
Weekly rebuilds increase deployment frequency and regression risk.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Container and runtime isolation
status_rationale: No container platform or runtime exists.
target_answer: Workloads run as containers on a managed orchestrator or platform where Echelon does not operate the control plane. Admission policy enforces: images only from Echelon's registry with verified signatures and provenance; non-root user; read-only root filesystem; no privileged mode, host networking, host path mounts or added capabilities; resource limits set. Each image has an SBOM (CycloneDX) generated at build. Tenant data isolation does not depend on container boundaries, since all tenants in a cell share the same application release (RR-UNB-PLAT-008-r1); dedicated-infrastructure tenants run in separate clusters or cells.
intended_practice: Select platform; write admission policies; generate SBOM and signed provenance in the build.
provable: Nothing. No production environment, configuration or operating evidence exists.
customer_statement: Planned: signed, non-root, read-only containers enforced by admission policy, with an SBOM per image. Not yet implemented.
residual_risks: Container escape vulnerabilities in the shared kernel remain possible on shared nodes (MITRE ATT&CK T1611).
open_questions: Will Unbound run on a container orchestrator, a serverless container service, or a platform-as-a-service? Each changes who controls admission policy.

title: Immutable infrastructure and pipeline-only change
status_rationale: CNV-PLT-010 requires signed builds with recorded provenance and two-approver review for control-relevant modules; not implemented.
target_answer: Production is never modified interactively. Every change to application or infrastructure is a reviewed commit, built by the pipeline into a signed artifact with recorded provenance (CNV-PLT-010; SLSA build provenance), and deployed by replacing running instances. Workloads have no shell access in production; diagnostic access is through logs and the brokered process in ANS-NET-005. Emergency changes use the same pipeline with an expedited approval path, never a console edit. Rollback is a redeploy of a prior signed artifact.
current_practice: Not established. Praxis provides repository provenance records and CI workflow, but it is not operated for any production service.
intended_practice: Make the pipeline the only identity with production write permissions; record each deployment as an evidence event.
provable: Nothing for production. Praxis provenance records exist for repository work (praxis@12bf9951) but not for deployments.
customer_statement: Planned: production changes only through a reviewed, signed pipeline with no interactive server changes. Not yet implemented.
residual_risks: The pipeline and its signing key become the critical asset; compromise of the build system yields signed malicious artifacts.

challenge.customer_intent: Customers want unauthorized or untested changes kept out of production and want a record of every change.
challenge.adverse_outcome: An unreviewed change introduces a vulnerability or a fraud path.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Change tickets and CAB approvals document intent but do not prove what actually ran; manual server changes routinely escape tickets.
challenge.legally_required: Not by statute. SOC 2 CC8.1 requires authorized, tested, approved changes, not a specific mechanism.
challenge.contractually_required: Contracts often require a documented change management process.
challenge.historical_convention: Change advisory boards date from shared, fragile infrastructure.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Removing interactive access and making the pipeline the only writer eliminates the unrecorded-change path within the production scope.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Signed artifacts and admission policy reject anything the pipeline did not build.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Each deployment emits provenance, approvals and artifact digests automatically (SOC2-004).
challenge.stronger_alternative: Pipeline-enforced review and signed deployment instead of ticket-based approval.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, by matching running image digests to signed provenance.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Any retained console write access, unsigned deploy path, or break-glass used for changes.
challenge.conventional_cost: CAB meetings and ticket overhead per change.
challenge.alternative_cost: Pipeline engineering and signing infrastructure; low recurring.
challenge.alternative_risks: Fast deployment can propagate a bad change quickly; requires progressive rollout and rollback testing.
supporting_arguments: Proves what ran, not only what was approved.
Scales with AI-assisted engineering where change volume is high.

agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely with auditors familiar with continuous delivery; some bank reviewers still ask for a CAB.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Two-person review on all control-relevant modules (CNV-PLT-010) is harder with a very small team.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Infrastructure as code and policy as code
target_answer: All cloud resources, network rules, identities, key policies and managed service settings are defined in version-controlled infrastructure as code, reviewed like application code, with policy-as-code checks (no public data stores, encryption required, approved regions only, logging enabled) run on every change before apply. Control-relevant infrastructure (network boundary, key policies, identity) requires two approvers, neither the author (CNV-PLT-010). Plans and applied changes are retained as evidence. AI agents may propose infrastructure changes but cannot approve or apply them.
intended_practice: Choose IaC tool compatible with the provider and Echelon's .NET/F# toolchain; codify guardrails before first resource is created.
provable: Nothing. No production environment, configuration or operating evidence exists.
customer_statement: Planned: all infrastructure defined as reviewed code with automated policy checks before any change is applied. Not yet implemented.
open_questions: Which IaC tool and state backend will be used, and where is IaC state (which can contain secrets) stored and encrypted?

title: Configuration drift detection and baseline evidence
target_answer: The IaC definition is the baseline. A scheduled reconciliation compares live cloud configuration to IaC state at least daily and on every provider configuration change event; any drift raises a control exception and is either reverted automatically (for guardrail settings) or reviewed within one business day. Provider configuration change logs are retained in the security log account. Evidence is the continuous drift report, not a periodic screenshot.
intended_practice: Implement drift detection with IaC; classify which drift is auto-reverted.
provable: Nothing. No production environment, configuration or operating evidence exists.
customer_statement: Planned: continuous comparison of live configuration against reviewed code, with drift raised as an exception. Not yet implemented.

challenge.customer_intent: Customers want assurance that systems stay in their approved secure configuration.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Silent misconfiguration, such as a storage bucket made public, exposing data.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Periodic configuration reviews catch drift weeks or months late and sample only part of the estate.
challenge.legally_required: No statute prescribes a review frequency; SOC 2 CC7.1 expects detection of configuration changes that introduce vulnerabilities.
challenge.contractually_required: Questionnaires ask for quarterly or annual configuration reviews.
challenge.historical_convention: Manual reviews were the only option before configuration APIs.
challenge.architectural_elimination: With IaC as the only change path and auto-revert of guardrail settings, most drift cannot persist.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Reconciliation runs automatically and reverts guardrail drift.
challenge.continuous_evidence: A daily drift report with zero-drift attestations replaces sampling.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, through reconciliation logs and provider change logs.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If console access allows changes outside IaC without event-based detection.
challenge.alternative_cost: Low; tooling is largely provider-native or open source.
challenge.alternative_risks: Auto-revert can undo a legitimate emergency fix applied out of band; emergency path must update code first.
supporting_arguments: Detection in hours instead of quarters.

agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely; continuous monitoring is widely accepted as satisfying periodic review if evidence is retained.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Some customers' policies literally require a documented periodic review by a named person.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Production access and environment separation
status_rationale: Operator access requirements exist (CNV-ARC-002, UNB-XIN-IAM-005); no environments exist.
target_answer: Production is a separate cloud account with no human standing write access. Engineers and AI agents work only in non-production environments that contain synthetic data; production data is never copied to non-production (SOC2-031 requires production and synthetic evidence to be kept distinct). Read diagnostics in production are scoped, expiring and sponsor pre-approved; writes require per-case approval (CNV-ARC-002). Production database administrative roles are break-glass with two-person activation (CNV-PLT-010). Access grants and every use are evidence events, and quarterly access reviews are generated from those events.
intended_practice: Implement account separation and access broker with the hosting decision.
provable: Nothing. No production environment, configuration or operating evidence exists.
customer_statement: Planned: no standing production access for engineers or AI agents, no production data in non-production, and per-case approved access. Not yet implemented.
residual_risks: A very small team makes two-person rules and separation of duties hard to staff; the residual risk is concentration of privilege in one or two people.
open_questions: How many people will hold production break-glass capability at launch, and who are the second approvers?

title: Supported component lifecycle and end-of-life management
status_rationale: Strata supports PostgreSQL 16 only (current-state brief); CNV-ARC-004 makes Strata version support a precondition for database upgrades. No component register exists.
target_answer: Every runtime component (.NET runtime version, base OS image, PostgreSQL major version, Strata release, managed service versions) is listed in a component register with vendor support end dates. Releases fail if a component is past end of support or within 90 days of it without an approved upgrade plan. For PostgreSQL, the upgrade path is gated by Strata support for the target version (CNV-ARC-004) so the platform cannot be stranded on an unsupported database version. Unbound targets the current .NET long-term support release.
current_practice: Not established. Known constraint: Strata is PG16-only, and PostgreSQL 16 community support ends in November 2028 under the PostgreSQL five-year policy.
intended_practice: Create the register from the SBOM and deployment manifest; add the support-date gate.
provable: Nothing beyond the Strata version constraint documented in the current-state brief.
customer_statement: Planned: an automated register of component support dates that blocks releases on unsupported components. Not yet implemented.
residual_risks: If Strata does not add support for newer PostgreSQL versions in time, Unbound faces a choice between an unsupported database and replacing Strata, which CNV-ARC-004 and UNB-TEC-STRATA-001 make a binding selection.
open_questions: What is Strata's roadmap for PostgreSQL 17 and later support?
Verify the PostgreSQL 16 end-of-life date against the PostgreSQL versioning policy page before relying on it in customer answers (not re-verified in this session).
